purpose: Close the characteristic-two loophole left by v0.8. The NP-hard rank<=3 affine-nonsingularity carrier lives over GF(2), whereas the v0.8 coefficient proof used characteristic zero and division by 2.

model.rank_r_update: M -> M + U V^T, with U,V having r columns and r>=2.
model.one_core_local_augmentation: N=[[M,U R],[L V^T,D]], where the top-left block contains exactly one copy of M and D,L,R are independent of M and all untouched Boolean variables.
model.target: det N = det M + det(M+UV^T) as a polynomial identity over GF(2).

theorem.name: NO_CHAR2_ONE_CORE_FACTORED_RANKR_BOOLEAN_ELIMINATION_FOR_R_GE_2
theorem.statement: Over GF(2), no one-core local augmentation of the frozen factored form can realize det M + det(M+UV^T) for any r>=2.
proof: It suffices to consider invertible M and put K=V^T M^{-1}U. Schur complementation gives det N=det(M) det(D+L K R).
The matrix determinant lemma gives det(M+UV^T)=det(M) det(I_r+K). Therefore the target requires det(D+LKR)=1+det(I_r+K) for every K.
In characteristic two the right-hand side has zero constant term and linear part tr(K), because det(I_r+K)=1+tr(K)+terms of degree at least two.
Hence det(D)=0. If rank(D)<=s-2, every (s-1)-minor of D vanishes, adj(D)=0, and the determinant has zero linear part under every perturbation, contradicting tr(K). Thus rank(D)=s-1.
For a corank-one square matrix D, adj(D) has rank exactly one.
The linear part of det(D+LKR) is tr(adj(D) L K R)=tr(R adj(D) L K). Its coefficient matrix in the entries of K is H=R adj(D)L and therefore rank(H)<=1.
The target linear form tr(K) has coefficient matrix I_r, whose rank is r>=2. Equality of the linear forms is impossible. Contradiction.

two_adic_corollary.statement: The same frozen one-core factored identity cannot hold over Z/2^k Z for any k>=1 and r>=2.
two_adic_corollary.proof: Reducing any such identity modulo 2 would produce the forbidden GF(2) identity above. Thus powers-of-two arithmetic do not rescue this local Schur model.
